name: NewInterfaceDialog
intent: Author a shared ontology interface: name, description, status and what it extends.
when: Declaring a contract several object types will implement
Any create flow over a named, extendable type
whenNot: Adding a property shared across types -> use NewSharedPropertyDialog
Grouping types for navigation -> use NewTypeGroupDialog

chooseOver.because: It offers the Extends picker and can enforce the description rule, which is the difference between an interface and a name.

requireDescription.note: Enforce the best-practice description rule. Default false, so existing hosts are unchanged.

dataContract.rowIdentity: Drafts carry no id; the host mints one on accept.

states.default: Name and API name, status at its default.
states.extending: One or more parent interfaces chosen.
states.strict: With requireDescription, creation is refused until a description is given.

evaluationCriteria: requireDescription defaults false so existing hosts do not change behaviour.

lineage.authoredBy: Promoted in group C of the missing-widgets template review (2026-08-26)
notes: Its own comment records that it reproduces a private NewInterfaceDialog from a since-removed fork — exactly the duplication this promotion prevents.
Already an exported component with a typed props interface and no fixture coupling — this manifest is the only thing that was missing.

usage: Use NewInterfaceDialog when you need to display content that temporarily overlays the main interface. This component is useful for focused interactions, confirmations, or supplementary information.
NewInterfaceDialog should be used sparingly as overlays interrupt the user's workflow. Reserve this component for important interactions that require user attention or action before continuing.

anatomy.description: NewInterfaceDialog is composed of the following parts:

parts.name: NewInterfaceDialogTrigger
parts.description: Element that opens the dialog when activated.

parts.name: NewInterfaceDialogContent
parts.description: Container for the dialog content and overlay.

parts.name: NewInterfaceDialogHeader
parts.description: Header section containing title and description.

bestPractices.title: Focus management
bestPractices.description: Trap focus within the dialog and return focus when closed.

bestPractices.title: Don't nest dialogs
bestPractices.description: Avoid opening dialogs from within dialogs, use sequential flow instead.

bestPractices.title: Provide clear exit
bestPractices.description: Always include a visible close button and support Escape key.

bestPractices.title: Don't trap users
bestPractices.description: Never make dialogs impossible to close or require specific actions to dismiss.
bestPractices.example: // No close button or escape handling

bestPractices.title: Keep content focused
bestPractices.description: Limit dialog content to a single task or decision.

bestPractices.title: Don't overload dialogs
bestPractices.description: Avoid putting complex forms or multiple tasks in a single dialog.
